title: What they said at the time

clips.q: Firing 3,400 of arguably the most successful salespeople in the company could prove terrible for morale.
clips.who: **Colin McGranahan**, Sanford C. Bernstein, in a note quoted by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Mar 29, 2007[^30]

clips.q: Unfortunately, a number of Associates are directly impacted by the actions, but we are making Circuit City stronger for the long term.
This strategy strikes me as being quite cold.
Despite the significant consumer enthusiasm, we cannot create a viable business without support in these essential areas.
clips.who: **Richard L. Sharp**, on closing Divx, June 1999[^33]

clips.q: Based on market conditions and the completion of our initial due diligence process, we have determined that it is not in the best interest of Blockbuster’s shareholders to proceed with an acquisition of Circuit City.
clips.who: **Jim Keyes**, Blockbuster chairman and CEO, Jul 1, 2008[^35]

clips.q: We are extremely disappointed by this outcome.
They were too focused on Wall Street. That was the beginning of the end.
clips.who: **Alan Wurtzel**, at the University of Richmond, Oct 2012[^32]

clips.q: We were basically pushing our customers out the door, saying we don’t want to sell to you anymore.
clips.who: **Tom Wulf**, former Circuit City manager, on the appliance exit, 2013[^29]

clips.q: We thought we were smarter than anybody.
clips.who: **Alan Wurtzel**, to the Richmond Fed’s Econ Focus, 2013[^29]
